title: Accent marks and stress
about: Every word of two or more syllables carries one accent, and words of one syllable carry none, except *ή* "or", the question words *πού* and *πώς*, and a few others that need telling apart. The stress can never go further back than the third syllable from the end, which is why it moves forward in forms like *αγοράσαμε* and *των ανθρώπων*. A word stressed on its third-last syllable takes a second accent before a clitic: *το όνομά μου*.

items.en: How are you? We haven't talked in ages!

errs.why: One-syllable words take no accent: *τι*, *ναι*, *και*, *μου*, *το*. *Τι* is one of them.

items.en: Where do you live? Near the centre?

errs.why: The question word "where" is *πού*, with an accent; *που* without accent means "that, who, which".

items.en: Would you like tea or coffee?

errs.why: "Or" is *ή*, with an accent; *η* is the feminine article.

items.en: What's your name?

errs.why: The question word "how" is *πώς*; *πως* without accent means "that" (*είπε πως θα έρθει*).

items.en: My name is Dimitra.

errs.why: *όνομα* is stressed on its third-last syllable, so before *μου* it takes a second accent: *το όνομά μου*.

parts: Το σπίτι μου είναι κοντά στο σχολείο.
items.en: My house is near the school.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *σπίτι* is stressed on its second-last syllable, so *το σπίτι μου* takes no second accent.

items.en: Yesterday we bought a new fridge.

errs.why: The stress cannot be further back than the third syllable from the end: *αγόρασα*, but *αγοράσαμε*, *αγοράσατε*.

items.en: We're coming on the next bus.

errs.why: *έρχομαι* moves the stress forward when the word grows: *ερχόμαστε*, *ερχόσαστε*.

items.en: My car is at the garage.

errs.why: *αυτοκίνητο* is stressed on its third-last syllable, so before *μου*: *το αυτοκίνητό μου*.

items.en: Tell me how the accident happened.

errs.why: Here it asks "how", so *πώς*. Compare *μου είπε πως ήταν κουρασμένη* "she told me that she was tired".

items.en: The friend I introduced you to is an actor.

errs.why: The relative "who, that" is *που*, without accent.

items.en: Professors of foreign languages spoke at the conference.

errs.why: Feminine nouns in *-α* stress the genitive plural on the last syllable: *η γλώσσα* → *των γλωσσών*, *η θάλασσα* → *των θαλασσών*, *η ώρα* → *των ωρών*.

parts: Ο καθηγητής μας μάς έδωσε πολλές ασκήσεις.
items.en: Our teacher gave us a lot of exercises.
items.why: Nothing to fix: the first *μας* is "our" (after the noun); the second is "to us" before the verb and gets an accent, *μάς*, so the two cannot be confused.

items.en: Call me when you arrive.

errs.why: An imperative stressed on its third-last syllable takes a second accent before a clitic: *τηλεφώνησέ μου*, *κράτησέ το*.

items.en: The spelling of the name is wrong.

errs.why: The genitive grows by one syllable, so the stress moves forward: *το όνομα*, *του ονόματος*, *τα ονόματα*, *των ονομάτων*.

items.en: People's lives changed with technology.

errs.why: *άνθρωπος* moves the stress forward when the ending is long: *του ανθρώπου*, *των ανθρώπων*, *τους ανθρώπους*.

items.en: Our teacher is from Chania.

errs.why: *δάσκαλος* is stressed on the third-last syllable, so before *μας*: *ο δάσκαλός μας*.

items.en: We didn't grasp the size of the danger.

errs.why: *ο κίνδυνος* moves its stress in the genitive: *του κινδύνου*, *των κινδύνων*.

items.en: We signed up for a dance class.

errs.why: Passive aorists stress the second-last syllable in the 1st and 2nd plural: *γράφτηκα*, but *γραφτήκαμε*, *γραφτήκατε*.

items.en: At school everyone made fun of him for his accent.

errs.why: When *ο* and *ι* are pronounced separately and the stress falls on the *ι*, it takes both marks: *κοροΐδευαν*. Without them the reader would say *οι* as one sound [i].

items.en: The church clock stopped at three.

errs.why: No diaeresis when the accent is already on the first vowel: *ρολόι*, *τσάι*, *κορόιδο*. The accent alone shows the vowels are separate.

items.en: The struggle for women's rights continues.

errs.why: *η γυναίκα* has genitive plural *των γυναικών*, stressed on the last syllable.

items.en: The language of our ancestors still lives in place names.

errs.why: *ο πρόγονος* moves its stress forward: *του προγόνου*, *των προγόνων*.

parts: είπε να διαβάσουμε το τρίτο κεφάλαιο.
items.en: The teacher told us to read the third chapter.

errs.why: Without an accent *ο δάσκαλος μας είπε* reads as "our teacher said". To show that *μας* belongs to the verb ("told us"), it gets an accent: *ο δάσκαλος μάς είπε*.

parts: Πού και πού βγαίνουμε για φαγητό στην πλατεία.
items.en: Every now and then we go out to eat in the square.
items.why: Nothing to fix: in *πού και πού* "now and then" the *πού* keeps its accent.
